title: Your First kubectl Commands 🖥️
description: Interact with your cluster and run basic diagnostic commands.

slides.title: kubectl – Your Control Center 🕹️
slides.content:
# The gateway to your cluster

`kubectl` sends REST requests to the API server. Every object creation, inspection, or deletion goes through it.

Basic syntax:
```
kubectl [command] [TYPE] [NAME] [flags]
```
Example: `kubectl get pods`

quizData.question: What does `kubectl get nodes` do?

options.text: Lists all nodes in the cluster

quizData.explanation: `get` retrieves a list of resources; `nodes` shows the cluster members.

slides.title: Cluster Info & Status ℹ️
slides.content:
## First things to check

- **`kubectl cluster-info`** – endpoints of control plane services
- **`kubectl get nodes`** – node status (Ready/NotReady)
- **`kubectl get pods -A`** – all pods in all namespaces (`-A` or `--all-namespaces`)
- **`kubectl get namespaces`** – list of namespaces

Right after install, you’ll see only system Pods running in `kube-system`.

slides.title: Try it yourself
slides.content: Run these commands after your cluster is up:
slides.codeSnippet:
kubectl cluster-info
kubectl get nodes
kubectl get pods -A

slides.title: Namespaces – Virtual Clusters 🏢
slides.content:
## Organising Resources

Namespaces logically divide cluster resources. Default ones:
- **default** – where you deploy unless specified
- **kube-system** – system components
- **kube-public** – public info
- **kube-node-lease** – node heartbeats

Use `kubectl create namespace <name>` to make your own.

quizData.question: Which namespace holds core Kubernetes components?
quizData.explanation: kube-system contains the API server, scheduler, etcd, and other critical services.

slides.title: Describing Objects 🔍
slides.content:
## Getting detailed info

- **`kubectl describe node <node-name>`** – hardware, conditions, events
- **`kubectl describe pod <pod-name>`** – container details, volumes, events

Describe is your best friend for debugging.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Enable kubectl autocomplete

**bash:**
```
source <(kubectl completion bash)
```
**zsh:**
```
source <(kubectl completion zsh)
```

It saves tons of typing!

quizData.question: Which command shows detailed events for a specific Pod?
quizData.explanation: `describe` outputs status, conditions, and recent events of the object.
